description: This course is focused on introducing concepts the students should know about Calculus; the branch of Mathematics concerned with the calculation of instantaneous rates of change and the summation of infinitely many small factors to determine some whole. Particularly, the concepts of limits, differentiation, and their applications will be discussed with precision. Such that the students will be able to apply the concepts and theories they will learn in the field of astronomy. The course will also try to incorporate real life applications in research and technology of the topics to explore their utility not just in their course exams but also in life. Multiple readings of the material in advance are highly expected from the students.
references: Love, C. E., & Rainville, E. D. (1969). Differential and Integral Calculus, 6th ed. The Macmillan Company.
